description: Growing up in Singapore, where many are raised bilingual, Yung Raja found his voice between Tamil and English. By blending both in his music, he created a sound that reflects who he is, while introducing more people to his language and culture. author: TEDx Talks
description: In an iconic hawker centre in Singapore, five retirees started a small bookstore with a simple idea: to create a space for connection. Dakota Dreams shows how books became a reason for neighbours to gather, from seniors finding companionship to strangers becoming friends. Built on trust, generosity and care, it reminds us that community is not something we find, but something we create together. Dakota Dreams is a not-for-profit community bookstore founded by five retirees in the Dakota community. It celebrates local stories and brings neighbours together through children’s books, comics, and pre-loved titles by Singapore authors. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What If a Bookstore Could Build a Community? | Dakota Dreams  | TEDxSingapore GIS

author: TEDx Talks
description: Nikki Tan lends her voice to nature through film. From a fleeting encounter in the open ocean to the murky waters of Singapore, she reveals what often goes unseen. When we begin to see the life that surrounds us, we may start to care, and in caring, choose to protect what we once overlooked in our own waters. Nikki Tan is a Singapore-based conservation filmmaker whose work explores stories of our ocean and climate. Collaborating with climate NGOs and regional partners, she uses film to inspire action and strengthen impact storytelling across the region. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What Lies Beneath Our Waters? | Nikki Tan | TEDxSingapore GIS

description: Classical music is often tied to tradition and seen as serious. Foo Say Ming explores what happens when these ideas are reimagined through bold reinterpretations and collaborations. Through his group, re: mix, a petit ensemble of classically trained musicians, he brings new life to traditional and local works, showing how music can surprise, connect and evolve. Foo Say Ming is the music director of re: mix, an ensemble of classically trained musicians reimagining what classical music can be. Through inventive collaborations and bold reinterpretations, he brings new energy to the concert stage and invites audiences to experience music in fresh and surprising ways. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the biggest shift in your financial life didn’t start with a budget — but with honesty?

Alison Kosik explores why so many women avoid talking about money and how that avoidance can impact financial confidence, financial literacy, personal finance decisions, investing, and long-term financial security.

After years reporting on Wall Street, markets, and money, Alison realized that understanding the basics of personal finance isn’t always enough. Many women know more than they think,  but still feel disconnected, uncertain, or avoidant when it comes to their own finances.

Through 3 brave and revealing questions, Alison offers a practical framework to help women better understand their money habits, build financial confidence, and take back control of their financial lives.

This is about more than budgeting or investing. It’s about self-worth, confidence, and financial empowerment for women and what becomes possible when women stop avoiding money and start owning it.
 Alison K
title: Why Women Avoid Money — and How to Take Back Control | Alison Kosik | TEDxNaples

description: In a rapidly changing world shaped by technology, global challenges, and shifting social values, what does it truly mean to be human today—and how might that change tomorrow? In “The Evolution of Being Human,” this talk explores the journey of humanity through generations, reflecting on how our ideas of success, relationships, identity, and culture have continuously evolved over time. Focusing on Generation Beta, the first generation to grow up fully immersed in intelligent technology and constant connectivity, the talk examines the opportunities and challenges they may face. As information becomes instant and digital and physical realities merge, the real question may no longer be how to access knowledge, but how to think critically, build meaningful connections, and find purpose in a complex world. description: This talk explores the idea that the next generation may grow up inside invisible systems that quietly shape their choices. Drawing from a personal experience of temporary paralysis, I compare physical confinement to the subtle restrictions created by algorithms, AI, and over-optimised environments. The talk asks an important question: Are we building comfort at the cost of freedom? Ultimately, it challenges parents and society to ensure that the next generation knows where the doors of choice and individuality still exist. The talk challenges parents, educators, and society to rethink what progress truly means. Instead of eliminating these systems, the solution may lie in building doors within the walls; spaces where children can experience boredom, struggle, questioning, and discovery. This talk explores the idea that the next generation may grow up inside invisible systems that quietly shape their choices. description: Time isn’t an asset because it can be used to make more money or get degrees. It’s an asset because it is the only thing that will ever make sense the second you start to run out of it. People talk volumes about making their time count, but lack the action to do so. They fall into this abyss of thought where all they can think of is what another person in their life would say. This talk delves into the importance of living life as one intends to, stating that it will be the only thing that will ever matter. The message reflects a deeply human realisation: time is not simply something to manage - it is something to live. And the choices people make about how they spend it ultimately shape the story of their lives. Time isn’t an asset because it can be used to make more money or get degrees. description: Generation Beta – “Growing up between Algorithms & Emotions” highlights the unique reality of children born from 2025 onwards, who will grow up in a world deeply shaped by Artificial Intelligence, automation, and digital connectivity. The title reflects the balance this generation must maintain between advanced technology (“algorithms”) that guide learning, communication, and daily life, and the human values (“emotions”) such as empathy, relationships, ethics, and resilience. The title emphasizes that while Generation Beta will benefit from AI-driven education, global collaboration, and innovative problem-solving opportunities, they will also face challenges like digital dependency, privacy concerns, mental health pressures, and the need for ethical use of technology. Therefore, parents, educators, policymakers, and society must guide them to use technology wisely while nurturing human connection, creativity, and critical thinking. author: TEDx Talks
description:
¿Por qué un "no" rotundo suena a determinación en un hombre, pero a menudo se percibe como frialdad en una mujer? En esta charla provocadora, Ana Mallén pone sobre la mesa una verdad incómoda: la autoridad y el juicio firme han sido históricamente condicionados por el género.

Ana nos invita a desmantelar las exigencias adicionales de "suavidad" y las correcciones de estilo que se imponen a las mujeres en los espacios de toma de decisiones. No se trata de imitar modelos masculinos, sino de reclamar el derecho a ejercer un criterio profesional sin penalizaciones sociales. A través de una visión clara y contundente, Ana demuestra que la competencia es el único estándar que debería importar y que, al final del día, la firmeza no tiene género. Ana Leticia Mallén es Directora de la Licenciatura en Innovación y Negocios en la Universidad de la Libertad en México. Es doctora en Sociología y ejecutiva senior en ESG y sostenibilidad, con más de una década liderando proyectos estratégicos en in
title: Cuando la autoridad suena a mujer | Ana Mallen | TEDxToluca Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
En el mundo de la ciberseguridad, a menudo se nos enseña a construir muros y ocultar debilidades. Sin embargo, Lorena Bravo descubrió que su mayor fortaleza no radicaba en la infalibilidad, sino en su capacidad de ser vulnerable. En esta charla, Lorena nos lleva por su proceso de reinvención personal y profesional, desde su destacada carrera en Google hasta el momento en que decidió aceptar quién es realmente.

Lorena relata cómo, al abrazar su propia vulnerabilidad, logró encontrar a su "tribu" y dar vida a WomenCISO, uno de los movimientos de mujeres en tecnología y ciberseguridad más grandes de Latinoamérica. Es una historia sobre el coraje de quitarse la armadura para construir puentes, demostrando que el liderazgo más poderoso es aquel que se atreve a ser auténticamente humano. Lorena Bravo, líder en Ciberseguridad, IA y Transformación Digital en LATAM. Reconocida por El Heraldo de México entre las 25 más influyentes por equidad.
Fundadora Google Security Practice LATAM.
Creadora
title: El poder de la vulnerabilidad | Lorena Bravo | TEDxToluca Women

description:
¿Es necesario encajar en los moldes tradicionales de liderazgo para construir una empresa exitosa? Mariana Velásquez, fundadora de Branddu, nos demuestra que la respuesta es un rotundo no. En esta charla, Mariana comparte su viaje desde la creación de su empresa hasta los retos monumentales de escalarla en un entorno empresarial que a menudo ignora la visión femenina.

A través de su experiencia personal, nos revela cómo los obstáculos que enfrentó como mujer líder se convirtieron en la base de su fortaleza y en el motor de innovación para su marca. "Lead Like a Woman" no es solo un título, es una invitación a liderar con autenticidad, a abrazar la intuición y a entender que el crecimiento de un negocio y el desarrollo humano van de la mano. Una plática esencial para emprendedores y directivos que buscan una nueva perspectiva sobre el poder y la gestión de equipos. Mariana Velásquez, emprendedora serial con +17 años en merchandising. description:
Quien domina la palabra, domina su libertad. Esta charla explica por qué la oratoria y el debate son las herramientas que nos permiten pensar por nosotros mismos, no ser manipulados y defender nuestras ideas sin depender de nadie. Porque la verdadera libertad empieza cuando puedes razonar, argumentar y decidir con claridad.

 Juanjo García Amorós es empresario, abogado y profesor universitario, especializado en argumentación, oratoria y debate. Doble Graduado en Derecho y ADE, ha sido diez veces Campeón Nacional de Debate y doble cuartofinalista mundial, además de haber recibido una decena de premios al "Mejor Orador" en diversas competiciones nacionales. En 2026 ha sido incluido en la categoría Ones to Watch del prestigioso ranking internacional Best Lawyers, que reconoce a los profesionales con mayor proyección en el ámbito jurídico. author: TEDx Talks
description:
¿Qué sucede cuando dejamos de ver a la tecnología como una herramienta y empezamos a verla como un reflejo de nuestra propia humanidad? En esta charla, Karim Espejel, fundadora de Mente Colectiva, nos invita a cambiar la narrativa del miedo a la automatización por una de "Humanidad Aumentada".

Karim, quien combina su formación como psicóloga con una sensibilidad artística desarrollada en la Compañía Nacional de Danza Folklórica, nos propone un viaje fascinante: usar la IA no solo para optimizar procesos, sino para fortalecer nuestro bienestar y pensamiento crítico. Con experiencia facilitando diálogos en foros globales y empresas de alto nivel, Karim demuestra que el verdadero reto de la era digital no es técnico, sino profundamente ético y humano. Es momento de mirar al espejo tecnológico y decidir quiénes queremos ser. Divulgadora de la relación humano-tecnología, psicóloga y fundadora de Mente Colectiva. Karim une conducta humana e innovación digital, especializándose en IA ética

author: TEDx Talks
description:
¿Puede aquello que más te aterra convertirse en el símbolo de tu éxito? En esta charla, la reconocida diseñadora mexicana Tanya Moss nos lleva por un viaje de metamorfosis personal y profesional. Lo que comenzó como una fobia infantil a las mariposas terminó siendo el emblema de una de las marcas de joyería más importantes de México, recordándonos que nuestros miedos pueden ser nuestros peores enemigos o nuestros mejores aliados.

Desde los juegos en el clóset de su abuela hasta el momento de revelación en un taller de joyería en el extranjero, Tanya comparte cómo la persistencia y el apoyo familiar la ayudaron a superar el bullying y la timidez. Con casi 29 años de trayectoria, Moss reflexiona sobre los retos de emprender en México y la importancia de la coherencia y la honestidad al poner tu propio nombre en una marca. Una historia sobre evolución, resiliencia y el poder de las joyas para contar quiénes somos. Tanya Moss ha sido apasionada por la joyería desde niña. Su trabajo fusio
title: ⁠Diseñar Alas, Construir Sueños: Ser la CEO de tu Propia Historia. | Tanya Moss | TEDxToluca Women

Uma reflexão sobre autenticidade, identidade e a decisão de ser a própria permissão para viver com verdade. Porque a linha nunca foi real. A permissão sempre foi sua. terapeuta Xamânica, comunicadora, treinadora comportamental, e fundadora do Instituto Origem de desenvolvimento humano.
Por propósito, sou uma pessoa apaixonada por convidar outras pessoas a viverem sua própria natureza através do resgate de sua versão mais original e daquilo que é verdadeiramente essencial para sua alma. E acredito que uma evolução real passa necessariamente por uma revolução espiritual. author: TEDx Talks
description:
A economia da distração nos aprisionou no que chamo de "O triplo pedágio do tempo”, onde pagamos com nosso tempo em três partes: Primeiro, o pedágio da atenção: horas do dia indo embora em pequenos cliques. Segundo, o pedágio do trabalho: a gente trabalha pra pagar coisas que muitas vezes não eram prioridade, mas viraram desejo depois da exposição  repetitiva e estímulo.
E terceiro, o pedágio do pós-consumo: esperar, a entrega, organizar, manter, devolver… e, em alguns casos, lidar com golpes e fraudes. Se você também sente que o dia some sem perceber, eu quero conversar com você sobre isso. Sua experiência profissional culminou na fundação e CEO da Explore Close, uma startup de tecnologia que utiliza a IA e a neurociência para otimizar a "riqueza psicológica" do usuário, entregando recomendações de turismo e lazer hiperpersonalizadas que transformam o tempo livre em bem-estar. Esta missão é a solução prática para a "Mil e Uma Cobranças" que assola a sociedade.
Em sua trajetória pesso
title: O triplo pedágio do tempo. | Elizabeth Rocha Fernandes | TEDxItajaí
